articles.title: Premier League predictions & Jones Knows' best bets: More Andoni Iraola issues? Liverpool to slip at Ipswich
articles.summary: Our football betting expert Lewis Jones is back to preview the weekend card;Watch Ipswich vs Liverpool, Hull City vs Aston Villa, Everton vs Manchester United and Arsenal vs Chelsea all LIVE on Sky Sports; Play Super 6 to win £1m!
articles.body:
Ipswich vs Liverpool, Friday 8pm, live on Sky Sports

Liverpool could become the first club in history to have three £100m+ players on the pitch at the same time. That frightening statistic is playing a part on why they are as short as 1/2 with Sky Bet to break a run of six games without a win across the two seasons.

This is a packed squad, full of talent, but one that looks uncomfortable trying to implement Andoni Iraola's style. Nottingham Forest created 2.3 worth of expected goals at Anfield last weekend - the third-highest total a team has amassed in the last 77 Premier League home games. It makes them uneasy favourites on Friday night.

For a betting angle, eyes should be drawn to Leif Davis, who is 4/1 with Sky Bet to score or assist.

The flying full-back is playing almost as the left winger in this system, scoring at Manchester United to add to his two goals in pre-season. His assist capabilities are also very noteworthy - possessing a wand of a left foot, Davis has registered 21 assists in the last two Championship campaigns.

SCORE PREDICTION: 2-2 | JONES KNOWS' BEST BET: Leif Davis to score or assist (4/1 with Sky Bet)

Newcastle vs Bournemouth, Saturday 12.30pm

This could be a very fun game involving two managers who like to play fast, vertical football. Anthony Elanga looks a different player under Matthias Jaissle playing this style. His confidence is sky high and when he's in full flow he is such a weapon for a team that like to play direct balls - as seen by his goals against Liverpool and Spurs.

He's not always reliable in front of goal but is capable of these types of goalscoring streaks, so the 100/30 with Sky Bet on him to score again has potential.

Brentford have been arguably the most impressive Premier League team after two games.

The level of performance they put up in the win over Tottenham and draw at Leeds gives us some evidence to conclude that their process has improved since last season. This was on show in the first 60 minutes against Leeds where they were outstanding.

They created the most shots (15) and touches in the opposition box (31) any away team at Elland Road has produced in the opening 60 minutes since the start of last season.

Sunderland are difficult to make a case for, especially playing away from home where they have amassed an expected goals difference per 90 of -0.8 since the start of last season. Relegated West Ham and Wolves had better numbers than that.

To boost the Brentford win price, they've scored six first half goals in their three games in all competitions this season, being in front at the break in all three of them. I'm happy to back a repeat for Brentford to be winning at half-time and full-time at 6/4 with Sky Bet.

SCORE PREDICTION: 3-0 | JONES KNOWS' BEST BET: Brentford/Brentford at half-time/full-time (6/4 with Sky Bet)

Yankuba Minteh, Jack Hinshelwood, Kaoru Mitoma, Georginio Rutter and Mats Wieffer all could be missing for Brighton. It's why they've been weak in the betting in the build-up to this one.

Since Daniel Farke switched to a back three in December, Leeds have been very comfortable defending away from home and taking a very conservative approach to first halves.

Not many goals are being scored to the extent that five of their last six away games have been 0-0 at half time. The 7/4 with Sky Bet for another 0-0 at the break is a runner.

There is lots of volatility from a prediction point of view for this encounter which has become a big match for both managers as they look to get their campaigns moving in the right direction.

Palace have lost the defensive identity that made them so successful under Oliver Glasner, while the attacking improvements have not yet materialised consistently. Fulham fans are already frustrated with Alvaro Arbeola after their timid showing at Sunderland. A low-scoring draw it is.

Manchester City vs Coventry, Saturday 3pm

Manchester City were like clockwork in these types of spots under Pep Guardiola. Normally victories over newly-promoted teams are achieved with minimal fuss, meaning those looking to add a City win to their weekend accumulators shouldn't have too many sweaty moments.

Rayan Cherki at 5/6 with Sky Bet for another assist will be popular. The French maestro is averaging 0.45 assists per 90 since the start of last season - a ratio hotter than Bruno Fernandes. In a game where City are expected to score three goals, backing Cherki is the way smarter way to back a pro-City angle.

Nottingham Forest vs Tottenham, Saturday 3pm

It must be so stressful being a Spurs fan. Seriously, how can they be this bad still after spending so much this summer?

They were more competitive last weekend in the defeat to Newcastle but they were so easy to score against and there is still a feeling that the players are weighed down by past failures.

Tottenham have attempted an enormous tactical and personnel reset whilst Forest do have more continuity and have shown signs of implementing Glasner's style. They were more like a Glasner team at Anfield, secure and organised without the ball but also so dangerous to stop when they decided to press forward almost as a front five with the full-backs pushing on.

There is an expectation that Morgan Gibbs-White's output is going to grow under this manager and he got off the mark at Anfield. He's had at least a shot on target in his last four starts against Tottenham and averages 1.05 per game since the start of last season. Combining him to have a shot on target and Forest to avoid defeat rates as a decent wager at 10/11 with Sky Bet.

Hull vs Aston Villa, Saturday 5.30pm, live on Sky Sports

Hull have won their opening two games and are yet to concede a goal. Of course, they've done it with the backdrop of losing the expected goals battle in both matches. Some things never change.

However, as someone who lives and dies by the data from an analytical point of view there remains a strong possibility that the Tigers will hit a wall in terms of their form. It should start here.

I'm anticipating Unai Emery to get Aston Villa going again pretty sharpish.

September is his favourite month. His record in September in the Premier League is just one defeat from 18 matches, winning 11.

Emery has also never lost a game with Villa against a promoted side, winning 15 of the 21 matches and in their last nine games away from home against a newly promoted side they have scored 23 goals. The 17/20 on offer for the away win with Sky Bet is one of the best bets of the weekend.

SCORE PREDICTION: 0-2 | JONES KNOWS' BEST BET: Aston Villa to win (17/20 with Sky Bet)

Everton vs Manchester United, Sunday 2pm, live on Sky Sports

Everton endured a Deadline Day to forget. However, although they have a weaker squad, their starting XI may actually be stronger than what the market assumes.

And playing Manchester United at home could be exactly what they need right now. A proper siege mentality game is classic David Moyes where the fans will be on board with the pragmatic approach to get a result. Remember, it's the hierarchy who they have turned on - not the players or Moyes.

Ipswich competed well with United up until Harry Maguire's controversial goal which then allowed Michael Carrick's team to flow and take advantage of lots of space.

Everton are almost the opposite opponent to Ipswich. They will make this very difficult.

Arsenal vs Chelsea, Sunday 4.30pm, live on Sky Sports

Are the market giving enough respect to Arsenal here?

The home win at 4/6 with Sky Bet is going to tempt a lot of punters in.

Arsenal will make this a typically Arsenal game where they look to control transitions, defend with ultra organisation and take advantage when their moments come. They'll be confident of stopping the Chelsea front three, who have been electric but it's too early to be calling them a serious team.

Just one clean sheet in their last 18 Premier League games identifies that.

In that same 18-game run Arsenal have kept 10 clean sheets. Levels.

This is also a defence which has kept 11 clean sheets in their last 14 home games, conceding just three goals in their last 13 home games in all competitions.

We don't need to overcomplicate matters here. Arsenal to win and under 3.5 goals has landed in 10 of the last 14 games at The Emirates. It's Evens to go in again.

1pt on Leif Davis to score or assist (4/1 with Sky Bet)

1pt on Brentford/Brentford (6/4 with Sky Bet)

articles.title: Derby County: Takeover collapse took wind out of sails, says Stephen Pearce
articles.summary: Owner David Clowes remains committed to financing Derby despite having been an hour away from selling the club, says Rams CEO Stephen Pearce.
articles.body:
Owner David Clowes remains committed to bankrolling Derby County's Premier League promotion ambitions despite having been an hour away from selling the club, says Rams chief executive Stephen Pearce.

Clowes, a Derbyshire property developer and lifelong Rams fan who took the club out of administration in the summer of 2022, was poised to hand over ownership of the Championship side to Saudi Arabia government official Turki Al-Sheikh in August.

Despite an agreement being reached, and the deal being sanctioned by both the Independent Football Regulator (IFR) and the English Football League (EFL), Al-Sheikh suddenly withdrew his interest.

Pearce said the weeks it took for the bid to be scrutinised left Derby in a "holding pattern" for a large part of the summer transfer window and added that the collapse of the deal was "completely out of the blue".

"The wind was taken out of our sails, totally," Pearce told BBC Radio Derby.

"We weren't expecting it to fall down, effectively, an hour before we thought it was going to complete.

"But we regrouped and everybody got back on the horse. It was like, right how do we go again? And let's crack on with what we wanted to do."

Derby and Clowes were well positioned to do exactly that, with the Rams owner having already signed off on a budget and committed to signings while the takeover attempt was unfolding.

The £6m it took to bring Bobby Clark in on a permanent deal from RB Salzburg, the loan to buy agreement to get Sam Szmodics for £2.7m from Ipswich, and the sum of around £600,000 it took to get Alex Mowatt from West Bromwich Albion were all funded by Clowes when he thought he was about to sell the club.

"This is why he's such an incredible owner. He thought the takeover was going to happen, he knew he was never going to get a penny back for all of that money he spent on those players and he still did it," Pearce said.

"He could have quite easily, on 1 July, said to us and said to John [head coach John Eustace], 'look, I think this is going through, the signs are the club is going to be sold, you're just going to have to wait because every penny I put in into transfers now I'm not going to get back'.

"And he didn't. He backed it regardless and that's why we're such a strong position."

Clowes had long been open about his desire to bring in new investors to help fund the club's push to return to the Premier League, and the agreement with Al-Sheikh – who, alongside being a Saudi government official, is a hugely influential figure in the world of boxing - had been seen as a significant boost for a side that finished just outside the play-off places last season.

When the takeover failed, Clowes took Derby County off the market and focused efforts on strengthening the club he nearly offloaded.

The £4m spent on getting David Ozoh from Crystal Palace was the biggest outlay - alongside a list of free transfers and loans, which included a deadline day reunion with Eiran Cashin - after the aborted deal.

Asked if the disrupted summer had "stalled" the club's aims of Premier League promotion, Pearce replied: "Not in the slightest, otherwise we wouldn't have spent all the money we've spent.

"We want to push on. We want progression this season."

articles.title: The number 10 shirt must not retire with Messi
articles.summary: Maradona and Messi each made the shirt their own. The next great Argentinian player should have that chance, too.
articles.body:
When Lionel Messi announced his retirement from the Argentina national team last Monday, the reaction bordered on national mourning. Children cried in schools, journalists shed tears on television, newspapers filled their pages with emotional tributes and a telephone line was even opened for fans to express their gratitude to their idol. All weekend matches in Argentina were briefly stopped in the tenth minute as a tribute to the idol.

“I emptied myself. I have nothing more to give,” Messi wrote in his farewell.

It was an extraordinary end to an extraordinary relationship. For more than two decades, Messi had carried the expectations of a country that could never quite decide what it wanted him to be. He was compared endlessly with Diego Maradona, criticised for not displaying the same kind of passion and, for years, accused of somehow being less Argentinian because he had left for Barcelona as a child.

Yet by the time he walked away, the relationship between Messi and Argentina had been transformed. The player once treated as an outsider had become a national symbol in his own right.

“And we are full,” Jorge Valdano, a World Cup winner with Argentina in 1986, replied to Messi’s farewell. Messi may have emptied himself, but Argentina was full of everything he had given it.

Messi played 207 official matches over 21 years with his national team, an entire lifetime. He scored 125 goals and provided 68 assists. With him on the pitch, Argentina began every match with almost a goal guaranteed. He played in six World Cups, won one in Qatar in 2022, and reached two other finals. The last came less than two months ago in the United States, where, at 39 years old, he had his most productive World Cup, scoring eight goals and providing four assists.

His last great display came in the semifinal against England in Atlanta. Argentina trailed until the final minutes before staging a spectacular comeback to win 2-1, one of the most celebrated victories in the history of the national team.

For Argentina, beating England has never been just about football. The rivalry is inseparable from the dispute over the Malvinas Islands and the 1982 war. After the semifinal, the players unfurled a defiant anti-colonialist banner asserting Argentina’s claim. Beating England means beating the old Empire. And for Argentinian football, it inevitably evokes another number 10: Maradona, whose defining 1986 World Cup included that other historic victory over England.

Messi’s own victory over England would prove to be his last great display. Four days later, there was little left. Exhausted, he was barely involved as Spain dominated the final but needed extra time to win 1-0. “My legs gave out on me,” he later wrote in a public letter to his father, who died 20 days after the match.

Much of the international press accused Messi and Argentina of “not knowing how to lose”. As Spain received the World Cup a few metres (feet) away, the Argentinian players remained on the pitch with their backs turned towards the ceremony, after a few of them had been involved in a brief but ugly confrontation following the match.

The scene was not pleasant. But look at it through Messi’s eyes, and it becomes something else. He stood still, tears in his eyes, looking towards the supporters who loved him. What others saw as gracelessness in defeat was also a farewell. Messi already knew that this was goodbye. And, for the first time, his dying father could not be there with him.

Messi had once been criticised relentlessly in Argentina because, for all his success elsewhere, he spent more than a decade failing to win a major title with the national team. He even walked away from it once, in 2016, before coming back. Today, he leaves as a symbol of persistence, a rarity in times when everything is fleeting.

His departure has also prompted calls for Argentina to retire the number 10 shirt in his honour.

The Argentine Football Association (AFA), which published an emotional farewell video, will not do so. In official competitions, FIFA’s squad-numbering rules make that impossible. Argentina has been here before.

When Diego Maradona died in 2020, during the social isolation of the COVID-19 pandemic, the grief was overwhelming. “I would steal Maradona’s coffin and carry it through every neighbourhood of poor kids … until the sun, the rain, the earth and the wind turned it into ashes that would fly across the entire territory of the homeland,” the poet Liliana Campazzo wrote at the time.

There were calls then, too, to retire the number 10. But doing so would have taken the shirt away from Messi, who had worn it for Argentina since 2009 and was still writing his own history in it.

That matters because in Argentinian football, the number 10 has never been just a squad number. Traditionally worn by the great creative player, it became a distinction reserved for the true genius of the team. Maradona gave it eternal significance after Mexico 1986. Messi then made it his own.

Pele had already made the number 10 synonymous with footballing genius on the world stage, and generations of great players followed. But nowhere has the shirt carried quite the same weight as in Argentina, where it passed from Maradona to Messi.

Maradona and Messi played in 10 of the last 12 World Cups in which Argentina competed. Each won one: Maradona in 1986 and Messi in 2022. Between them came three more appearances in World Cup finals: Italy 1990 for Diego, Brazil 2014 and the United States in 2026 for Leo. Together, they scored 29 World Cup goals.

The numbers tell us how much Argentina owed them on the pitch. They do not explain what each came to mean beyond it. And the two men could hardly have been more different.

Diego was all excess, generosity and caprice. Millions of Argentinians became his “emotional slaves”, as the Spanish journalist Ramon Besa once wrote. Leo, by contrast, has always been far more reserved, perhaps because he witnessed Diego’s decline at close quarters and saw the price of fame.

Messi did not inherit Maradona’s number by becoming another Maradona. He carried the same enormous expectation in an entirely different way and, eventually, made the number his own. Whoever comes next will have to do the same.

These are days of mourning and orphanhood for the national team. Argentina has lost Maradona, and now, from the pitch at least, it has lost Messi. But Argentina has always been a factory of great players, and football lives on the hope that there can always be another.

In Spanish, we say “no hay dos sin tres”: “There is no two without three”. There is no third yet. Perhaps there never will be another Maradona or another Messi. But retiring the number 10 would mean giving up on the possibility.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Roundtable: Don't leave the party without 'em — Our analysts share their must-draft player for 2026
articles.summary: Don't leave your fantasy football draft without one of these top choices from our analysts.
articles.body:
The biggest fantasy football draft weekend of the year is upon us as we prep for the 2026 NFL season, which begins next Wednesday. You've likely been consuming as much content as humanly possible to be in the best shape going into your draft. But there's always more! If there's one thing you do at your draft, it's select these players. Yahoo analysts Chris Allen, Hayden Winks, Josh Norris, Scott Pianowski, Joel Smyth, Justin Boone, Matt Harmon and Ray Garvin give you their one must-draft player for 2026.

Chicago's passing game has garnered most of our attention all offseason. And rightfully so, with Year 2 of the Ben Johnson-Caleb Williams connection upon us and the rise of Luther Burden III. But D'Andre Swift's role in all of this has gone under-discussed. Swift had a career year after being reunited with his old OC. Most would look at 1,386 regular-season all-purpose yards as a "mid" result. But a look under the hood tells a better story.

Among all RBs in 2025, Swift's 51.0% rushing success rate ranked fourth. Coupled with top-12 marks in adjusted yards after contact per attempt and explosive play rate, Swift had the base-down work secure. Plus, only six other RBs took more carries from inside the five-yard line than Swift. All of this came while playing through multiple lower-body injuries, which only caused him to miss one game. So now, Swift is (mostly) healthy, Johnson considers Kyle Monangai's knee hyperextension a week-to-week issue and there's less uncertainty around the offense. If we're going to treat all of the pass-catchers as early-round picks to target, Swift deserves the same consideration. — Chris Allen

After about 200 drafts, my most drafted player is Etienne with a personal ADP of 40th overall. On Yahoo, Etienne is a consensus fourth-round selection with an ADP of 42nd overall as the RB18. I rank him 33rd overall, so it's a full round of value early in drafts. Etienne is coming off an RB11 per-game finish on RB14 usage. That was while splitting work in Jacksonville, and we'll see just how much Alvin Kamara can play as a 31-year-old with a training camp multi-week knee injury. Etienne will safely be the goal-line back and has a pass-catching history on early downs dating back to college.

This Saints team quietly provides the best environment he's had for fantasy points. Head coach Kellen Moore was first in neutral pace rate last year, and the offensive line features two quality first-round tackles, a newly-signed veteran LG and two long-time teammate interior players. It's an above-average unit, and Etienne is used to bottom-10 OLs from Jacksonville. He's cleared 1,399 total yards in three of four healthy seasons, and I think he'll do it again. — Hayden Winks

My season rides on a handful of players. Namely: Saquon Barkley, Kenneth Walker III, De'Zhaun Stribling and Parker Washington. Simply put, the Jaguars WR1 has been undervalued all summer long. Washington is currently being drafted 74th overall on Yahoo, when his real price should be closer to 55th. With Washington, Jakobi Meyers and Brian Thomas Jr. on the field together last season, PW had a team-high 31% target share with 3.17 yards per route run. So if you have any questions about how this "loaded" receiver room is going to play out, we already have our answer.

In that same section of the season, Washington played 63% of his snaps from the slot when all three receivers were on the field together. That's exactly what we want, as he attacks the precise area that Liam Coen's offense emphasizes: 10-20 yards over the middle of the field. Washington wins small with his athleticism. He wins big on tight-window targets. And if he were a second-round pick in the NFL Draft rather than a sixth, Washington's ADP would be multiple rounds earlier. — Josh Norris

McConkey was a dominant player in the second half of his rookie year , but everything fell apart in Year 2. I'll write that off as an excused absence — the offensive line collapsed, the play calling went stale and the target tree was crowded. Mike McDaniel steps in as the perfect OC — a creative schemer who will put McConkey in motion and find YAC-producing routes downfield. Keenan Allen is gone, so the target tree is trimmer. QB Justin Herbert can be a talent elevator, especially now that the line is fortified again (despite the loss of starting center Tyler Biadasz). McConkey is still available outside of Pick 40 in Yahoo leagues, a delightful buying opportunity for the final draft weekend. — Scott Pianowski

Round 2 has plenty of RBs available, and my favorite at ADP is Omarion Hampton at 18th off the board. Talented RBs going into their second season are consistently fantasy gold. In fact, of the first 11 RBs drafted inside the top-25 since 2015, all 11 of them had a fantasy RB1 season by their second year. Ashton Jeanty and Hampton are up next.

When healthy, the Chargers' RB was a force as a rookie, posting RB1 fantasy numbers in an overall poor situation. I love the coaching change as much as the talent. Mike McDaniel has had a top-seven fantasy RB in three consecutive seasons, and even with the 11th-best scoring offense since 2022, has the third-most RB fantasy points. If a 31-year-old Raheem Mostert can be a top-five fantasy RB with McDaniel, I'm betting Hampton can, too. He'll get the goal-line work and showed great receiving chops as a rookie to the point where the Chargers only threw to RBs when he was on the field. Healthy offensive tackles and FB Alec Ingold can help the run game improve in the new system.

There are some that worry about Hampton's volume, but I trust he'll get the touches that matter most and plenty of work in an offense that I'm buying in 2026. — Joel Smyth

Smith is finally out of A.J. Brown's shadow and ready to prove he can be the Eagles' No. 1 receiver. Over the last two seasons, there have been three games where Brown was sidelined and Smith played a full complement of snaps. The results were stat lines of 6-84-0, 7-79-0 and 7-76-1 while averaging just under 10 targets per game. Even with Brown finishing as a top-12 fantasy wideout in recent years, Smith still produced as the WR17 (2024), WR21 (2023) and WR16 (2022) on a per game basis before this past season, when he was as the WR33 amid some overall struggles in the offense.

Fortunately, there are plenty of signs pointing to the Eagles having a bounce-back campaign, including their new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, some better offensive line health and a very soft schedule. The 27-year-old (turns 28 in November) will enjoy the easiest slate at his position . Don't be surprised when Smith finishes as a fantasy WR1. — Justin Boone

Ever since the NFL Draft closed and we filed our first pass of rankings, I've had Waddle as my WR12 or 13 and a top-30 overall player. While I will grant you that Waddle has a frustrating injury history, to me, that's the only hole in his profile. There is so much the fantasy industry doesn't understand about Waddle and the situation change he's about to experience. Waddle ranks 18th in yards per route run and 13th in first downs per route the last three seasons. The only reason he didn't pop off last year without Tyreek Hill for most of the year was the Dolphins ranked 30th in neutral dropback rate and 32nd in plays per game. Denver ranked sixth and fifth — there will be much more raw opportunity awaiting, along with a quarterback upgrade.

The other often-missed variable is that Waddle has long been playing out of position as an outside on-ball receiver in Miami to allow for role-catering for other players. Going to Denver with Courtland Sutton established as the X-receiver and Pat Bryant emerging as the big, on-ball slot, Waddle is about to play a movement Z-role for the first time in years. I can't even say how much of a game-changer this is going to be for the new Broncos receiver. He's going to run more breaking routes and get a ton of layups running routes off the line. He will be a big hit player as a Round 4 pick that returns WR1 value. — Matt Harmon

I'm betting on the Year 2 leap with Tetairoa McMillan. As a rookie, he showed that he can be the clear No. 1 receiver in an NFL offense, and there's no question who the best wideout in Carolina is. Yes, there are concerns with Bryce Young and the offensive line, but McMillan should continue to command a massive share of this passing game regardless. He earned a 25% target share as a rookie and accounted for 43% of Carolina's air yards. Now I want to see the Panthers make life easier on him. If Jonathon Brooks can give them a legitimate running game, that should create better opportunities off play action, and I'd love to see McMillan used more from the slot to manufacture easier looks. All indications point to Carolina doing exactly that with him in the offense. My projections have him around 145 targets and 1,250 yards. At a Round 4 price, I'm buying the talent, the volume and the Year 2 breakout. — Ray Garvin

articles.title: Empiezan los sacrificios en el Barça
articles.standfirst: El doble pivote, con muchas alternativas y sobrado talento
articles.summary: El doble pivote, con muchas alternativas y sobrado talento
articles.body: El Barcelona tiene una plantilla competitiva. En todas sus líneas. Pero el talento y las opciones que acapara en su doble pivote es la envidia de LaLiga y del fútbol mundial. Este fin de semana, Hansi Flick tendrá que empezar a hacer sacrificios. Para su satisfacción. Pedri, Gavi, Marc Bernal y Rodri ya están a disposición del técnico alemán. Los cuatro se disputan los dos puestos en el eje de la medular, una vez el centrocampista andaluz se sumó ayer jueves a las sesiones tras superar la contusión que sufrió en el primer encuentro de LaLiga en Elche, salió de inicio junto al catalán, y que el madrileño ha adquirido ritmo de entrenamientos y minutos: intervino en 27 y 26 contra el Athletic y el Rayo respectivamente. Bernal es el único que ha disputado los tres primeros encuentros del torneo nacional regular: fue titular en los tres, pero no los completó. En los dos últimos, que arrancó junto a Pedri, cedió su puesto a Rodri. El ex de Las Palmas sólo fue suplente en el Martínez Valero al incorporarse más tarde a los entrenamientos azulgranas por la disputa del Mundial. Pero para el compromiso de este domingo en Mestalla, Flick ya dispone de los cuatro. Todos tienen un gran talento aunque le ofrecen cualidades y variantes de juego distintas. La idea principal del preparador azulgrana es apostar, a lo largo del curso, por Pedri y Rodri de titulares, por su estilo y liderazgo. Pero Gavi, que también puede moverse en otras posiciones, y Marc Bernal han demostrado sobradamente sus recursos para pelear por el puesto. El preparador germano no ha definido del todo aún su once contra el Valencia, aguardará a la última sesión, pero no descarta esperar unos días más para apostar por Rodri de inicio y confiar en él, junto al canario, en el exigente estreno de Champions League que les espera a los culés la próxima semana: el miércoles reciben al Feyenoord en el Spotify Camp Nou. "Disfrutaremos con ellos jugando juntos. Disponer de ambos nos permitirá controlar el balón y al rival. Es algo muy importante", reconoció Flick hace unos días sobre el doble pivote que los dos internacionales pueden formar a lo largo de la temporada. "Todo el mundo está contento de que Rodri juegue en el Barça. Es perfecto para nuestro estilo. También tenemos a Marc Bernal en esa posición. Rodri tiene más experiencia, es el líder claro. Es uno de los mejores", comentó Hansi Flick sobre el madrileño en los últimos días. La temporada es larga y el técnico dará minutos a los cuatros, pero en las próximas horas, deberá hacer sus primeros sacrificios en una ubicación en la que, además, también puede colocar a Eric García, Olmo...

articles.title: British journalist Piers Morgan calls Messi’s GOAT ad the ‘most arrogant’ and ‘shameless’ bragging ever
articles.summary: Football News: Piers Morgan criticizes Lionel Messi's latest advertising campaign for Michelob Ultra, branding it the 'most arrogant' display in sports history amidst the ongoing Messi-Ronaldo GOAT debate. Discover his true sentiments following Messi's international retirement.
articles.body: Lionel Messi may have just retired from international football, but apparently the Messi-Ronaldo GOAT debate did not get the memo.The Argentina legend has been at the centre of the argument for years, and his latest appearance in a Michelob Ultra advertising campaign has given Piers Morgan another reason to make his own feelings known. The advert turns Messi's remarkable international career into a giant bar receipt, ticking off his goals, assists, minutes and major trophies before ending with a rather cheeky verdict: "GOAT debate-settled."Morgan, a long-time Cristiano Ronaldo supporter, was not particularly impressed.Messi's career becomes a bar tabThe Michelob Ultra campaign shared on Messi's Instagram takes a playful approach to his Argentina career, presenting his achievements as though they have been added to a restaurant or bar receipt.Instead of simply listing his honours, the advert runs through the numbers and milestones that helped define his time in the famous blue and white shirt. His goals, assists and minutes are all included, while the list also highlights his biggest international achievements, including the 2022 FIFA World Cup, multiple Copa América titles, Olympic gold and the Finalissima.It even nods to the millions of fans Messi has inspired throughout his career before arriving at that final line: "GOAT debate-settled."Importantly, that was the advertising campaign's conclusion rather than Messi personally declaring himself the greatest player ever.That distinction did not stop Morgan from having his say.The British journalist, who has repeatedly backed Ronaldo in the long-running debate, described the campaign as "the most arrogant piece of shameless bragging in the history of sport" and called it "Hilarious" in a post on social media.It was a typically strong reaction even from someone who has made no secret of where he stands.Morgan used Messi's retirement to make the Ronaldo caseMorgan's latest comments came just days after Messi announced his retirement from international football, bringing the curtain down on a 21-year Argentina career.The 39-year-old leaves with 207 appearances and 125 goals, making him Argentina's record appearance-maker and leading goalscorer. His international career ultimately delivered the major prizes that had once seemed to elude him, including the World Cup and Copa América.His retirement followed a difficult few weeks. Argentina lost to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final, Messi's second defeat in a World Cup final after the 2014 loss to Germany, while his father, Jorge Messi, died at the age of 68 just weeks later.Ronaldo also reached out to Messi following the death of his father, offering a more personal message amid the difficult period.Commenting on Instagram, the Portugal captain wrote: "A huge hug to you and your loved ones during these difficult times, Leo. Stay strong."The message offered a reminder that, despite the fierce comparisons between the pair and the constant debate among their supporters, Ronaldo and Messi have maintained mutual respect throughout their careers.Morgan responded to the retirement announcement on August 31 by immediately turning the conversation towards Ronaldo."Breaking: Lionel Messi retires from international football, after scoring 125 goals for the Argentina national team, placing him second on the list of highest international goalscorers," Morgan wrote.He then followed it with the comparison he clearly wanted to make."Cristiano Ronaldo has scored 146 goals for the Portugal national team, the highest figure in the history of football at international level. This settles the debate over who is the best player in history," he added.Morgan has previously left Messi out of his all-time XI despite the Argentine's eight Ballon d'Or wins and extraordinary collection of team honours. He has also named four players he considers better than Messi.His position is hardly surprising given his long-standing friendship with Ronaldo, and the two superstars have spent much of their careers being compared with one another.Even with Messi now stepping away from international football, it seems that particular argument is going nowhere. If anything, it has found a new receipt.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: Malas noticias para Mattéo Guendouzi. articles.title: Clemson officials notify LSU it may be breaching contract if it plays former pro players Saturday
articles.summary: Clemson leaders have spent the last several days conducting an examination of the game contract, which includes an article prohibiting the participation of i...
articles.body:
Clemson officials notified LSU that the participation of former professional football players on Saturday may breach the game contract between the schools.

In a brief email sent Friday afternoon to LSU's general counsel, Clemson general counsel Chip Hood made it clear that the school intends to travel to Baton Rouge and play in Saturday's season opener, but he addresses "certain eligibility" issues that may break "contractual obligations between the two parties." The obligations are "not relieved by the ongoing disputes," according to the email, obtained by Yahoo Sports.

The university is not seeking financial damages or in no way suggests filing legally against LSU. However, Clemson emphasizes that it "supports the position of the NCAA and our conferences regarding the eligibility of professional athletes returning to play college sports."

Clemson administrators and legal counsel have spent the last several days conducting an examination of the game contract, which includes an article prohibiting the participation of ineligible players.

LSU has not taken action to formally add pro players to its roster, but a Louisiana judge on Thursday paved the way for such a possibility , granting a group of athletes a preliminary injunction for a fifth season of eligibility, including players who signed pro contracts and have committed to join coach Lane Kiffin's team.

In an interview with Yahoo Sports on Thursday, South Carolina Attorney General Alan Wilson expressed strong feelings toward any professional athletes taking the field against his state school.

"This is about fairness," he said. "If LSU wants to change the rules for those players, they can petition the SEC to request a waiver, but going to the courts. … Think of the parade of horribles. If LSU wins, every other SEC school can go to their courts and get a different judge to say something. You'd have total chaos and anarchy."

Wilson declined comment on Clemson's examination of the game contract as he had not reviewed it himself. That said, he believes the SEC, as a private organization, should be allowed to govern itself and enforce its rules, especially a bylaw approved by all 16 university presidents. LSU president Wade Rousse voted to reaffirm the conference's ban on pro players just last week during an in-person meeting in Birmingham at the league office.

"Once you become a professional athlete, you are banned. All other schools are abiding by this rule," Wilson told Yahoo Sports.

Wilson is scheduled to travel to Baton Rouge for the game, which is certain to be a tense environment for the visitors. "I may have to up my security when I go down there!" he said with a laugh.

Clemson's email serves as the latest chapter in what's been a drama-filled storyline over the last several weeks.

On Thursday, in an unprecedented move for the conference, the SEC filed a federal lawsuit against LSU, its president, board and athletic director, asking a judge to grant it injunctive relief to permit the league to enforce its rules against LSU, if the school was to violate conference bylaws by rostering professional athletes. Within the lawsuit, the SEC claims that LSU and coach Lane Kiffin "orchestrated [a] campaign to recruit professional athletes to join the LSU football roster."

The program has public commitments from at least three players who signed professional contracts and received injunctions to return to college as part of the lawsuit, including ex-Ole Miss players Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris. Their impending additions to the roster — the players said Thursday they expected to be added — would not only violate the SEC's rule against pro players but also stands to break the league's policy against players transferring from one conference member to another outside of the transfer portal window.

While Wright, a tight end, has already been practicing with the team, LSU has not clearly stated that it will add the players to its roster. Schools are required to submit their 105-man rosters to the College Sports Commission a day before the season opener — in this case, presumably at midnight ET Friday. However, teams can add players to the roster during the season as long as they left spots open, according to an SEC bylaw adopted in April.

A Louisiana judge on Thursday not only granted the players an injunction but enjoined LSU as a defendant in the case, along with both the NCAA and SEC, meaning the Tigers are prohibited from actions that negatively impacted the athletes — as in deciding against adding the players to the roster after promising them spots. An attorney for the players, Ryan Downton, told Yahoo Sports on Thursday night that he would ask the court to hold LSU in contempt if the program declined to roster his plaintiffs.

The ruling continues the public legal feud between the school and its own conference — an unprecedented fight, but only the latest amid college sports' rudderless landscape .

As reported on Monday on Yahoo Sports , SEC presidents have been exploring a variety of serious measures against the school if it adds former pro football/basketball players, including a boycott, probation, suspension and expulsion.

At the center of the league's aggressive approach to LSU is what leaders describe as a necessary defense of conference-wide rules. This is perhaps the first test of a long-discussed new model that SEC leaders are exploring — a league-only governance model where the conference, not the NCAA, creates and enforces policy as a way to limit legal challenges.

The SEC's approach to the LSU situation is a clear sign that the conference believes it must vigorously defend its rule or else risk the collapse of any league-wide governance concept before it's even established.

Sankey himself took it seriously enough to appear in court.

In an act indicative of the current state of the industry, the SEC commissioner spent more than three hours of the first week of the football season on the stand testifying during the preliminary injunction hearing in Louisiana.

Sankey is not expected to attend the Clemson-LSU football game Saturday. Kickoff is scheduled for 7:30 p.m. on ABC.

articles.title: Auburn has fallen. Alex Golesh is betting he can pick the Tigers back up
articles.summary: Auburn has spent years searching for a way out of the wilderness. Now Alex Golesh has arrived with a simple mantra: Be who you say you are.
articles.body:
AUBURN, Ala. — Every new regime starts with a mantra, and for Alex Golesh at Auburn, that mantra is, "Be Who You Say You Are." It's a helpful guidepost, a way to bring oneself in line with both expectations and assumptions.

But "Be Who You Say You Are" has been one hell of a challenge for the Auburn Tigers lately. Five straight years of losing records, plus six straight Iron Bowl losses, plus multiple embarrassing coaching departures, have the Auburn Family both seething and exhausted. It's now Golesh's job to remake both a team and an image.

"It's his only saying," says Auburn general manager Andrew Warsaw, who's now on his third stop with Golesh. "That's what he's always said, even when he was the [offensive] coordinator of Tennessee. If you've got a wide receiver who says, 'I'm going to be the best wide receiver,' cool. Do everything it takes. Go do it. If you're going to say it, be it."

Golesh and several of his assistants recently sat down with Yahoo Sports for wide-ranging conversations on the state of the Auburn program and the challenges of resuscitating a moribund brand in a hyper-competitive conference in a time of unprecedented college football chaos, a feat not unlike changing the tires on a car that's doing laps at Talladega.

Whether Golesh can manage the feat remains to be seen, but he gives off the aura of a man absolutely ready for the challenge, starting with his overarching philosophy: "Really clear and definitive direction, meaning every single standard in the program is clear, concise, defined. There's zero gray," he says. "When you walk out of the room, there's zero gray … on the expectation, the standard, the tactical, technical way that we're doing it. And I'm going to hold you to that standard."

Auburn's entire existence is a long run of grays, skyrocketing highs followed by plummeting lows. Only three SEC schools — Alabama, LSU and Georgia — own a more recent national championship than Auburn, and yet Auburn has exactly one 10-win season since 2013. It can make cases for putting two players — Cam Newton and Bo Jackson — on college football's Mount Rushmore, and the Tigers ran 109 yards to glory against Alabama with the Kick Six, arguably the greatest play in college football history.

But just as frequently, the school has embarrassed itself with scandals, incompetence and general mediocrity. (Win totals for the last six seasons: 6, 6, 5, 6, 5, 5.) The Loveliest Village on the Plains has one of the great celebrations in college football — rolling the Toomer's Corner oaks at the northeast edge of campus — but in the 2020s, the trees have remained mostly TP-free. It's now up to Golesh and the new-look Tigers to give the oaks the postgame decor they deserve.

The son of Russian parents who escaped the collapsing Soviet regime, Golesh arrived in Brooklyn in 1991 at age 7 with little knowledge of English or America itself. In short order, he shed his Russian accent, reveled in unfamiliar delicacies like bananas and Coca-Cola, and dove deep into the glorious sport of football.

Golesh's family moved to Ohio, where he played football at Dublin Scioto High School and went on to serve as a student assistant at Ohio State under Jim Tressel. And so he began the long, thankless, inglorious path of the wandering coach, working his way up through the ranks — co-offensive coordinator at the University of Central Florida, tight ends coach at both Iowa State and Illinois, running backs and tight ends coach at the University of Toledo. His work at Tennessee as offensive coordinator from 2021 to 2022 — a run which coincided with the Vols' resurgence and a notable win over Alabama — put him in position for a head coaching gig.

Golesh then took over a 1-11 South Florida team and led the Bulls to three straight bowls, finishing with nine wins last season and a brief appearance in the AP Top 25 at No. 18. That performance ensured his name entered the pool of candidates for big-dog jobs, and as luck would have it, Auburn had kicked Hugh Freeze to the curb after two-plus less-than-inspiring seasons. Conventional wisdom had Golesh headed to Arkansas as Auburn pursued Jon Sumrall. But Sumrall went to Florida, the Tigers tabbed Golesh, and here we are.

"In today's landscape, it's important that you search out the real ones from the fake ones," says tight ends coach Larry Scott, who gave up a head coaching job at Howard to join Golesh's staff. "He's a guy that earned it the right way. Came up in the business the hard, right way. And that speaks volumes to the type of person that he is, the type of man that he is. Those are the type of people you want to attach yourself to. People that are real, got their feet on the ground, down to earth."

Golesh, 42, signed a six-year, $44 million deal with Auburn, with considerable escalators involved. If he can get the Tigers to nine wins, for instance, he'll earn another $1.5 million, and a CFP berth will be worth $1 million.

Auburn introduced Golesh via a miniature version of its cross-campus gameday Tiger Walk, with fans lining Donahue Drive to welcome in the new coach and his family. The joy on that December afternoon was obvious, but so too was the message: Give us a reason to keep cheering . In his initial press conference, Golesh did exactly that.

"We're going to build a process-driven program: A process-driven program where we wake up and worry about winning every single aspect of our lives every single day," he declared. "A lot of the time you don't control the end result. You control your daily habits, your daily process. And if you keep pouring into that day in, day out … the process will pay you back. We're also going to have a hell of a lot of fun doing it."

"He's going to work harder than anyone, he's going to know every element of a program, he's going to be confident," says Warsaw. "He's going to build a culture, from a staff perspective and an athlete perspective, that people can buy into."

It's easy to look at Auburn's woeful recent record and roll your eyes at that. This is a program whose primary characteristic over the last decade-plus is an unerring ability to step on its own tail, whether giving up back-breaking last-second touchdowns in the Iron Bowl or gagging with an epic upset over Georgia on the line . There's a pall of fatalistic gloom that hangs over The Plains, and motivational slogans delivered at high volume can only do so much against that dark cloud.

Here's what Golesh does have working in his favor, though: the Auburn Family. Auburn fans take immense pride in that descriptor, a folksier collective term than, say, "Nation" or "Army" or whatever. The Family is annoyed right now, yes, but the Family will always support you, particularly when you don't embarrass the Family. The 88,000-plus fans who still pack Jordan-Hare Stadium every home Saturday just want a reason to keep on cheering.

Golesh might be able to give it to them. He's bringing along 13 players from South Florida, most notably quarterback Byrum Brown. Last season, Brown became just the 12th player in college football history to throw for over 3,000 yards and rush for over 1,000 yards in a season. He's the latest in a line of speedy, aggressive quarterbacks Golesh has overseen, a number that includes Hendon Hooker and Joe Milton III.

Brown is, in many ways, the embodiment of Golesh's take-the-fight-to-the-defense philosophy, one he's honed over years as both a head and assistant coach. He runs a version of the veer-and-shoot offense derived from Art Briles at Baylor, spreading his offense nearly the entire width of the field and seeking out the overmatched defenders.

Golesh's teams work quickly; at Tennessee as an OC, and at South Florida as a head coach, his offenses have ranked in the top two in seconds per play in each of the last five seasons. The speed pays quick dividends. South Florida last year ranked fifth nationally in points scored (40.5) and third in total offense (488.5 yards).

Behind the scenes, Golesh has worked quickly, too. He's brought in more than 40 new staff members, along with 40 transfers and 21 high school commits. This team shares a logo with the one that's struggled throughout the 2020s, but not much else. In this era, though, what you did last year doesn't matter, it's what you can get done now — like, immediately — that matters.

"Curt Cignetti just showed you can [win a national championship] in two years," Golesh says. "Everybody — administratively, donor-based, and I think nationally, is like, 'Well, it can be done in two years.' On the flip of that is, you could point to [Indiana] and say, 'Here is the funding that they had, here was the model that they used, here was the support.' If the expectation is that, then match that. So it does go both ways a little bit."

Auburn begins the Golesh era this Saturday against Baylor in Atlanta. Because this is the SEC, the schedule doesn't get easy at any point. Road trips to both Tennessee and Georgia lurk, and Florida, LSU, Ole Miss and Alabama will all be headed to The Plains.

It's that final game that draws the most interest around Auburn. Golesh has taken to repeating the line legendary Tiger coach Pat Dye used when asked how long it would take to beat Alabama: "Sixty minutes." Catchy, yes, but the Iron Bowl will loom large in the Auburn Family's collective mind until Golesh can rack up another win. Auburn has only beaten Alabama twice since the Kick Six in 2013, and hasn't won in Tuscaloosa, site of this year's game, since 2010 — and the Tigers needed a Heisman-clinching comeback from Newton to do that.

That's for later, though. For now, Auburn has Baylor in its sights. A string of wins would be lovely for the Auburn Family, but they'll settle for a little dignity to start. And then we'll find out if Alex Golesh and the 2026 Auburn Tigers are who they say they are.

articles.body:
Clemson offered an apparent response to LSU on Friday regarding the possibility of former NFL players suiting up for LSU in their season-opening game against Clemson on Saturday night.

According to Ross Dellenger of Yahoo Sports, Clemson general counsel Chip Hood sent an email to LSU's general counsel in which he mentioned "certain eligibility" issues that may break "contractual obligations between the two parties."

Hood seemed to be referring to a Louisiana judge granting an injunction Thursday to players who are looking to return for a fifth year of college football after spending time in NFL training camps.

Judge Clears Path for Ex-NFL Players to Join LSU

The players, Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, have committed to play for head coach Lane Kiffin at LSU.

However, multiple conferences have enacted rules against former NFL players returning to play in college, including the SEC, which is home to LSU.

On Thursday, the SEC filed a lawsuit against LSU with a U.S. District Court in Alabama, alleging that LSU is violating the SEC's "First Amendment right of expressive association" by attempting to break the conference's rules against using former NFL players.

According to Dellenger, Clemson plans to play against LSU, and it did not threaten litigation or request damages in the email, but it pointed out to LSU that the game contract between the two teams features "an article prohibiting the participation of ineligible players."

Clemson's position is not surprising given recent comments made by head coach Dabo Swinney.

Earlier this week, Swinney gave his take on college teams pursuing former NFL players, telling reporters , "It's kind of embarrassing. Honestly, it's embarrassing that's where we are. I don't blame the kids, but people trying to take advantage of the system. It's embarrassing, but we've been there for a while."

Neither Wright nor Harris have been added to LSU's official roster yet, and Friday is the deadline for the school to do so.

Both Wright and Harris played under Kiffin at Ole Miss before Kiffin took the head coaching job at LSU.

Wright, a tight end, recorded 39 receptions for 635 yards and five touchdowns at Ole Miss last season before spending time with the Philadelphia Eagles and Cleveland Browns in training camp and the preseason.

Harris, a defensive tackle, had 58 tackles, nine tackles for loss and three sacks last season at Ole Miss. He was with the New Orleans Saints during training camp.

articles.title: Atleti-Barça: un traspaso imposible
articles.standfirst: Los verdaderos motivos por los que en el Metropolitano nunca se llegó a valorar un acuerdo con el club azulgrana por Julián Alvarez
articles.summary: Los verdaderos motivos por los que en el Metropolitano nunca se llegó a valorar un acuerdo con el club azulgrana por Julián Alvarez
articles.body: Mucho se ha hablado y escrito sobre el caso Julián. Todo el mundo presumía de conocer la verdad y la realidad de la situación se ha tergiversado hasta superar todos los límites. Al final se cerró el mercado y se cumplió lo que Miguel Ángel Gil repitió públicamente hasta en cuatro ocasiones: nunca se negoció con el Barcelona y el delantero sigue en la disciplina rojiblanca. Esta estrategia del club, respaldada desde el primer momento por sus accionistas mayoritarios, encabezados por Apollo Sports Capital, se mantuvo en todo momento a pesar de las voces teledirigidas que apuntaron hasta la saciedad hacia otro escenario muy distinto. Pero, ¿por qué el Atlético de Madrid decidió seguir tan firme en esa línea dura y se negó a negociar con el Barcelona? El club rojiblanco ha dejado claro a todo el que le ha querido escuchar que tiene una manera de actuar y negociar basada en una serie de valores fundamentales y en la ética profesional. Siempre han transmitido que para ellos la transparencia, el respeto entre instituciones y la coherencia deben guiar tanto la dirección estratégica como el día a día del club. Consideran que esta manera de trabajar maximiza el valor y la imagen del club. El club madrileño no se opone a mantener conversaciones y negociaciones con ningún club por sistema o por capricho. Insisten en que no es una cuestión de ego ni mucho menos un asunto personal, como se ha deslizado en numerosas ocasiones. Para el equipo que dirige el club, se ha tratado siempre de una “cuestión de principios, de respeto y de hacer las cosas bien”. En este sentido, apuntan que, si un futbolista que entra en los planes de los rojiblancos no está a gusto en el club, lo primero es valorar la situación e intentar acercar posturas. Sin embargo, si finalmente el jugador prefiere buscar otras opciones donde seguir su carrera, la manera de proceder pasa por fijar un valor de mercado, exigiendo transparencia en las negociaciones tanto al club interesado como al representante del futbolista. Si ambas partes no se suman a esta forma de actuar, el club corta radicalmente cualquier tipo de conversación. A partir de ahí, cualquier intento de presión va a obtener un rechazo frontal por parte del Atlético de Madrid. Los responsables del club transmiten abiertamente que esa apuesta por la transparencia y la coherencia garantizan unas potenciales negociaciones justas y dentro del mercado. Sin embargo, en opinión de los rojiblancos, el conjunto azulgrana hizo todo lo contrario. Negoció a espaldas del Atlético de Madrid, se dirigió al jugador antes de duelos directos la pasada temporada, lanzó mensajes falsos a través de portavoces mediáticos y utilizó todo tipo de estratagemas que nada tienen que ver con la manera en la que el equipo ejecutivo del club y su Consejo de Administración entienden que debe gestionarse una negociación. A nadie se le escapa que la postura del Atleti ha sido muy firme. En las oficinas de la entidad madrileña califican lo sucedido este verano como “un ataque muy sucio por tierra, mar y aire. El Barcelona ha actuado de forma impresentable desde el principio hasta el final. Siempre han sabido que así no iban a conseguir nada, pero aun sabiéndolo y admitiéndolo en privado, han decidido seguir engañando a sus aficionados, a su entrenador y a su propia plantilla hasta el último día”. Está claro que las relaciones quedan muy tocadas entre ambos clubes. En el Atleti trabajan para recuperar cuanto antes a un jugador “que ha sido utilizado y engañado” y que siempre ha tenido una forma de actuar muy profesional y comprometida. “Él, como nosotros, lo ha pasado muy mal con toda esta situación alimentada por mucha información falsa y muy mala intención”.

articles.title: Uno a uno del Real Madrid contra el Betis: valoración y comentarios
articles.standfirst: Análisis de la actuación de los jugadores y de Mourinho
articles.summary: Análisis de la actuación de los jugadores y de Mourinho
articles.body: Tres cambios en el once introdujo Mourinho para medirse al Betis respecto al equipo que inició frente al Málaga. Volvieron Dumfries (por Trent) en la lateral derecho, Konaté (por Rüdiger) en el centro de la defensa y Güler por Brahim en el centro del campo. Sorprende la segunda suplencia consecutiva de Bernardo Silva, sobre todo no pudiendo jugar el martes por sanción, y de la misma manera, la titularidad de Valverde, el único pivote disponible para la Champions. En portería y en el ataque, como siempre desde el comienzo de la temporada, sin cambios. PRIMERA PARTE: Poco trabajo, pero resuelto con seguridad. Detiene en dos tiempos un tiro de Antony. Despeje abajo en otro disparo de Antony que se envenenó tras tocar en un jugador del Madrid. Muy seguro en la salida de un balón aéreo. NOTA EN EL PRIMER TIEMPO: 6 PRIMERA PARTE: Jugando con profundidad por la banda, siendo siempre una referencia para encontrar una salida, y viviendo relativamente tranquilo atrás, sin problemas para frenar las incorporaciones de Fran García. NOTA EN EL PRIMER TIEMPO: 6 SEGUNDA PARTE: Fue sustituido por Trent en un intento de explotar mejor en ataque la banda derecha, donde neerlandés no terminaba de generar nada de peligro. NOTA FINAL: 5 PRIMERA PARTE: Transmitiendo poca seguridad. Pérdidas peligrosas e innecesarias en la salida del balón, despejes poco contundentes... NOTA EN EL PRIMER TIEMPO: 5 SEGUNDA PARTE: Queda condicionado por una amarilla en una falta a Fran García muy lejos de su sitio y en una acción sin ningún peligro. PRIMERA PARTE: En el 'modo defensa' que le exige Mourinho y rozando el gol hasta en un par de ocasiones. Fuerte en los duelos y metido en muchas batallas. Contundente en un duelo con el Cucho a la hora de proteger un balón al espacio. Remata un centro de Güler que le saca Valles con una gran parada. Buena cobertura para impedir un centro peligroso de Bellerín. Tuvo sus más y sus menos con Antony tras una falta a Cucho. Se le marchó ligeramente alto otro cabezazo peligroso a la salida de un córner. NOTA EN EL PRIMER TIEMPO: 8 SEGUNDA PARTE: Con el Madrid más dominador, muy certero en los pases filtrados buscando romper líneas y encontrar a los centrocampistas. PRIMERA PARTE: Sin mucha presencia ofensiva porque Antony y el Betis, que está muy volcado en ataque por su banda, le están exigiendo mucho en defensa. NOTA EN EL PRIMER TIEMPO: 6 SEGUNDA PARTE: Ganando más protagonismo en ataque. Eliminó por completo cualquier amenaza de Antony, que acabó siendo sustituido, y se mostró mucho más en área contraria para intentar generar peligro y superioridad. PRIMERA PARTE: No está pudiendo exhibir sus poderes en ataque porque el Madrid no ha terminado de tener el control del balón y del partido. Muy exigido en defensa. Recibió un pisotón del Cucho nada más arrancar el partido que lo deja dolorido. NOTA EN EL PRIMER TIEMPO: 6 SEGUNDA PARTE: Se pegó una paliza física importante para corregir todos los desajustes que se generaban ante la incapacidad del Madrid de controlar el partido. Se marchó sustituido en el 81' justo antes de habilitar a Parrott en el gol del Betis al quedarse descolgado a la salida del córner. NOTA FINAL: 5 PRIMERA PARTE: Cara y cruz. Dando equilibrio al equipo y atento y agresivo en las ayudas defensivas. Por el contrario, impreciso, poco fiable con el balón y con dificultades para darle intención y velocidad a la circulación del balón. Con problemas para dar salida al balón ante la presión bética. NOTA EN EL PRIMER TIEMPO: 5 SEGUNDA PARTE: Ve amarilla por un agarrón a Marc Roca y Mou no espera mucho para cambiarlo. Bien en defensa pero sin ninguna claridad y fiabilidad en la organización. NOTA FINAL:5 PRIMERA PARTE: Diez minutos de furia al final para maquillar un primer tiempo en el que estaba pasando desapercibido: gran pase a Vini para lanzarlo a la contra, un disparo ajustado, un cabezazo que le saca Valles, otro buen pase a Mbappé... NOTA EN EL PRIMER TIEMPO: 6 SEGUNDA PARTE: Buena asociación con Mbappé que acaba en un disparo del francés. PRIMERA PARTE: Brillante. Toda la luz en la oscuridad futbolística del Madrid la puso él. Acciones de calidad impresionantes con las que alimentó a su equipo en ataque. Gran control en un balón imposible de Konaté para poner a correr al espacio a Dumfries con un pase milimétrico. Asistencia de lujo a Huijsen en la primera gran ocasión del Madrid. Se le va un pase de la muerte a Vinicius que el brasileño, muy forzado, estrella en el palo. Otro control orientado maravilloso en el centro del campo dio inicio a una jugada prometedora del Madrid. Regate a Marc Roca y pase interior al que no llega Vinicius por poco. Da salida al primer toque a una contra peligrosísima del Madrid. Ve amarilla por una 'faltita'. NOTA EN EL PRIMER TIEMPO: 8 SEGUNDA PARTE: Se juega la segunda amarilla en una falta sobre Marc Roca. Mou tuvo que prescindir de su calidad para no arriesgar más ante una posible expulsión y estando en el punto de mira tras la acción en la que se pidió la segunda amonestación. NOTA FINAL: 7 PRIMERA PARTE: Su primer tiempo queda marcado por su doble fallo a portería casi vacía al borde del descanso. El resto del primer tiempo, fogonazos intermitentes. Buena incursión por la derecha que acaba en córner. Buena asistencia a Güler que lo habilita para una gran ocasión del Madrid. Tras varios amagues en el área estrella su disparo en un defensa del Betis. NOTA EN EL PRIMER TIEMPO: 5 SEGUNDA PARTE: Arrancada vertiginosa que finaliza con un disparo que se le marcha desviado. Muy activo, tirando muchos desmarques en busca de espacios para explotar su velocidad. PRIMERA PARTE: Sigue lejos de su mejor nivel, pero aún así tiene mucho peligro: estrelló un balón al palo en una posición forzada y asistió a Mbappé en el increíble doble fallo casi a puerta vacía. Insistente y ayudando a hundir al Betis atrás con su arrancadas y desmarques. NOTA EN EL PRIMER TIEMPO: 6 SEGUNDA PARTE: Entra en el 64' por Camavinga. SEGUNDA PARTE: Entra en el 64' por Dumfries. SEGUNDA PARTE: Entra en el 64' por Güler. SEGUNDA PARTE: Entra en el 81' por Valverde. PRIMERA PARTE: El equipo acabó bien, generando muchas ocasiones y mereciendo adelantarse en el marcador. El arreón final fue poderoso e hizo tambalearse al Betis. Pero hubo fases en las que el Madrid concedió mucho a un Betis que por momentos le discutió la posesión del balón y le inquietó. NOTA EN EL PRIMER TIEMPO: 6 SEGUNDA PARTE: Ve amarilla por protestar.

articles.title: Ceballos: "Estamos apurando para llegar al partido de Champions"
articles.standfirst: El utrerano no entró en la lista ante el Real Madrid, pero quiere estar el martes frente al Lille
articles.summary: El utrerano no entró en la lista ante el Real Madrid, pero quiere estar el martes frente al Lille
articles.body: Dani Ceballos está viviendo un día muy especial. Aunque no entró en la convocatoria de Pellegrini, ya que apenas sumaba un par de entrenamientos como verdiblanco, está disfrutando en su regreso a casa. El destino ha querido que el primer partido del Betis desde su fichaje sea precisamente ante el Real Madrid, lo que le está permitiendo reencontrarse con los que, hasta hace un par de meses, eran sus compañeros. Pero como ha asegurado en Movistar LaLiga, espera que el de hoy sea el primer y último partido que se pierda antes de volver a jugar. Quiere estar el martes en Francia. Su regreso al Betis: "Volver a mi casa es muy bonito. Estoy muy feliz y deseando poder jugar y demostrarle a todos el cariño que me brinda la afición en este último tiempo". Su saludo a sus excompañeros: "Es verdad que ha sido todo muy precipitado en mi llegada. Estoy conociendo todavía a algunos del cuerpo técnico, pero con compañeros del Madrid de los que no tuve tiempo de despedirme, habiendo estado muchos años con ellos, han sido muchos abrazos con cariño y con ganas de volver a verlos". No llegó a tiempo para jugar hoy: "No he tenido la oportunidad de hacer un entreno, solamente terminar el reconocimiento médico ayer. Estamos apurando para llegar al martes, al partido de Champions, y muy contento con la confianza que me han brindado todos mis compañeros, sobre todo el entrenador". Con ganas de jugar frente al Lille: "Por supuesto. Ya lo hemos hablado, esperemos ir; va a depender de las sensaciones que vayamos teniendo día a día en los entrenamientos, pero esperemos estar disponible para el martes". Qué le puede aportar al Betis: "Sobre todo experiencia. Tenemos un grupo muy joven, creo que puedo aportar también control de juego, pero sobre todo ilusión. Ahora es momento de trabajar, de demostrar a lo que he venido, que es hacer al club un poquito más grande. Estoy deseando empezar en el campo y demostrarlo". Volver a jugar con Isco: "Isco es un fenómeno. Contento de volver a jugar con él, con buenas sensaciones. Ojalá lo podamos tener sano durante todo el año, que será un disfrute para todos los béticos".

articles.standfirst: Courtois, Güler y Dumfries reclamaron en los primeros siete minutos que el esférico estaba falto de aire, lo que obligó al árbitro a cambiar hasta tres esféricos
articles.summary: Courtois, Güler y Dumfries reclamaron en los primeros siete minutos que el esférico estaba falto de aire, lo que obligó al árbitro a cambiar hasta tres esféricos
articles.body: No había corrido un minuto del encuentro en el estadio de La Cartuja cuando apareció el primer contratiempo del encuentro. El balón llegó a los pies de Courtois y el belga le comunicó al colegiado Hernández Hernández que el esférico estaba falto de aire. Fue ahí cuando se produjo el primer cambio de balón por el colegiado. No iba a ser el úiltimo. Minutos después, una falta de Bellerín sobre Vinicius iba a provocar las dudas de Güler. El turco cogió el balón para disponerse a lanzar y, junto al brasileño, volvió repitió la queja de Courtois acerca de la presión. Tras una breve comprobación y pequeña discusión, el árbitro volvió a cambiar el balón antes de que el conjunto de Mou lanzase de tiro libre. No se quedaría ahí la cosa. Pasado el minuto siete, un saque de banda iba a provocar de nuevo otra disconformidad. Esa iba a ser de Dumfries, que evitó dirigirse al colegiado y fue él mismo quien realizó el intercambio en la banda de La Cartuja. Tres cambios de balón que dieron inicio a un duelo con sabor a Champions en Sevilla entre Real Betis y Real Madrid.

articles.title: Fenerbahce's Matteo Guendouzi and Mason Greenwood banned after Lyon brawl
articles.summary: Fenerbahce midfielder Matteo Guendouzi gets a four-match European ban and is fined 50,000 euros after a brawl following the Champions League play-off win at Lyon.
articles.body:
Fenerbahce midfielder Matteo Guendouzi has received a four-match European ban - with two of those games suspended - and been fined 50,000 euros (£43,000) for his part in a brawl following their Champions League play-off win at Lyon.

Mason Greenwood, the Turkish side's English striker, has been given a one-match suspended ban which, like part of Guendouzi's, "is subject to a probationary period of one year" and fined 30,000 euros (£26,000).

Lyon goalkeeping coach Antonio Ferreira has been handed a five-match ban, with two of those matches suspended, for what Uefa said , external was "serious assault" in clashes which took place following Fenerbahce's win, which sent them through to the league stage with a 3-2 aggregate victory.

Guendouzi was punished for "insulting others present at the match, provoking spectators and for violating the basic rules of decent conduct".

Greenwood, who moved to Fenerbahce from Lyon's fierce rivals Marseille in the summer, was penalised for "violating the basic rules of decent conduct".

Both clubs were also fined 50,000 euros "for its team violating the general and basic rules of conduct".

Guendouzi at centre of brawl after Fenerbahce win

Former Arsenal midfielder Guendouzi, who played for Marseille between 2021 and 2024, was repeatedly booed by Lyon supporters during the match.

He appeared to taunt sections of the French home support following Fenerbahce's victory and team-mates ushered him away as tempers flared.

After the scuffle at full-time, Guendouzi was seen shouting "Allez l'OM" towards a pitchside camera, referencing Marseille.

Video circulating on social media also appeared to show an individual wearing a Lyon kit confronting the France midfielder as he made his way towards the tunnel, with security staff and members of both teams getting involved.

A melee then broke out in the tunnel between both teams.

Speaking after the game to reporters, Guendouzi said he felt "disrespected" by Lyon fans who were taunting him with "insults" about his family.

"If we can't celebrate the way we want afterward, I find that disappointing," he added.

"When you have 60,000 people insulting your family, your mother, your children, even before the game and no-one on the referee's side tells the crowd to be quiet.

"I know that in France, when this kind of thing happens, there comes a point where they'll talk to the fans to stop and maybe stop the match."

articles.title: Luis Enrique: Paris St-Germain boss agrees three-year contract extension
articles.summary: Paris St-Germain manager Luis Enrique agrees a three-year contract extension that will keep him at the club until 2030.
articles.body:
Paris St-Germain manager Luis Enrique has agreed a three-year contract extension that will keep him at the club until 2030.

The Spaniard, 56, has guided PSG to back-to-back Champions League trophies and three Ligue 1 titles since taking the helm in July 2023.

His previous deal was due to expire at the end of this season.

The news was announced by the club prior to Friday evening's home league fixture against Monaco .

PSG quartet Joao Neves, Willian Pacho, Lucas Beraldo and Senny Mayulu have also signed extensions to their playing contracts until 2031, while Fabian Ruiz has agreed a new deal taking him up to 2028.

articles.title: Las Palmas y Leganés se atascan en un empate sin goles
articles.standfirst: Las mejores ocasiones son pepineras, incluida la primera del debutante Morata, pero Caro y Luca Zidane sostienen el 0-0
articles.summary: Las mejores ocasiones son pepineras, incluida la primera del debutante Morata, pero Caro y Luca Zidane sostienen el 0-0
articles.body: Las Palmas y el Leganés no pasaron del empate sin goles en el Estadio de Gran Canaria en un encuentro con dos partes muy diferentes. El conjunto pepinero tuvo mayor presencia en el primer tiempo, donde tuvo las mejores ocasiones, incluida la primera del debutante Álvaro Morata, mientras los canarios, que dejan escapar así sus primeros puntos ante su afición, reaccionaron tras el descanso. El Lega tras este 0-0 sigue invicto, encadena tres partidos sin encajar goles y duerme al frente de la clasificación. El Leganés salió con mayor determinación y Morata ya avisó en el primer minuto, aunque Caro le negó el gol en una jugada que quedó invalidada por fuera de juego. Los visitantes manejaban mejor la pelota y encontraron espacios para acercarse al área de Caro. La ocasión más clara llegó cuando Zico Buurmeester estrelló en el larguero una potente volea tras una acción ensayada desde el córner. La UD sufría para construir y sus primeras aproximaciones llegaron principalmente a balón parado. Pero Naim volvió a rozar el 0-1 tras quedarse solo ante Caro, pero su disparo se marchó demasiado cruzado. La respuesta local apareció pasada la media hora: Miyashiro recibió en el segundo palo y su remate a bocajarro fue rechazado por Luca Zidane bien situado. El descanso llegó sin goles y con poco fútbol ofensivo La segunda mitad presentó otra cara. Las Palmas salió con más iniciativa y Miyashiro volvió a generar peligro nada más comenzar, aunque Lalo evitó el remate de Jefté en boca de gol. El conjunto local ganó presencia y el partido empezó a jugarse con mayor ritmo, aunque las ocasiones siguieron llegando con cuentagotas. Los cambios introducidos por ambos técnicos terminaron de abrir el encuentro y el Leganés encontró espacios para correr, pero Gharbi no acertó tras una buena asistencia de Morata y Álex Sancris, nadas más salir, estuvo cerca del gol con un disparo cruzado y, en el tramo final, Caro se convirtió en protagonista. El guardameta local sostuvo a la UD con dos intervenciones decisivas. Primero se impuso en un mano a mano ante Ignasi Miquel y después volvió a responder frente a Soko tras una rápida transición visitante. Las Palmas también tuvo sus opciones, con Iván Jaime aportando electricidad y buscando generar superioridades en los últimos metros. Sin embargo, ninguno de los dos equipos consiguió transformar sus mejores momentos en goles. El Leganés terminó amenazando más en los últimos compases, pero Caro mantuvo su portería a cero. El conjunto local tampoco encontró la acción definitiva y el encuentro acabó como empezó: 0-0. Un punto para cada equipo después de un duelo que tardó en despegar y que ganó intensidad, pero no eficacia, en su segunda mitad.

articles.title: Vincent Kompany ready to take on challenge from Schalke 04
articles.summary: Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany seems ready to get right back at it after the teams 4-1 victory over VfL Osnabrück in the DFB-Pokal earlier this wee...
articles.body:
Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany seems ready to get right back at it after the teams 4-1 victory over VfL Osnabrück in the DFB-Pokal earlier this week.

The Bavarians will travel to Gelsenkirchen for a match-up with Bundesliga returnee Schalke and Kompany is eager to see his team hit the pitch.

"I've played there a few times with City and HSV. It's an arena that we, and I, know well. We're considered favorites for tomorrow, but we shouldn't believe that. It always starts from scratch. A good performance against Osnabrück and Stuttgart doesn't automatically guarantee success against Schalke. Their anticipation for the first Bundesliga home game after three years is immense. They shouldn't be hungrier than us tomorrow," Kompany said (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ).

Bayern Munich is still working out some kinks, but will enter the match as a prohibitive favorite against Die Königsblauen . The head coach will be sorting through how to best align his squad for the game as the squad's depth will make it easier for him to rotate players.
