articles.title: Rutgers fan goes on epic WFAN rant following UMass loss: ‘Deplorable, despicable, horrible’
articles.summary: In his initial stint with Rutgers, Greg Schiano lifted the football program out of the depths of despair and turned it into a somewhat respectable team. His...
articles.body:
In his initial stint with Rutgers, Greg Schiano lifted the football program out of the depths of despair and turned it into a somewhat respectable team.

His second stint as head coach hasn't gone quite as well, and Thursday night's loss to UMass, a 29.5-point underdog , might have returned the program to the misery that came before him.

After losing to UMass, who snapped a 16-game losing streak against FBS teams with a win over the Big Ten school, Rutgers fans took to the internet and radio waves to voice their frustrations. But no one summed up their experience and feelings quite like Gus, who called into The Zach Gelb Show on WFAN.

"'m a 20-year season ticket holder," Gus told Gelb. "I've traveled all across the country and followed this team. I have tickets next week to go to Boston College for the Red Bandana game. I have an Airbnb booked for the Wisconsin game to go to Chicago to watch Manungai play on Sunday night. I'm done. I'm canceling everything. It's done.

"And it's not emotional. Taking the emotion out of it as best I can. I'm done. What I saw tonight was the most deplorable, despicable, horrible adjustments on defense, from being the worst team in football last year defensively to what they did this year and now what they did tonight. I'm done. I don't know what else to say. A 20-year season ticket holder. I'm done.

"Tomorrow I'm calling the athletic director. My opinion means nothing, but, you know, I'm done. And I'm sorry. I want to root for a hometown team. I want to root for a New Jersey team. Like you said, we have a great fan base. We have a great rooting section in my section, people that I've known for years. We're done."

Gelb then asked Gus if he felt Schiano, who is 31-42 since returning to Rutgers in 2000, should be fired.

"Absolutely," he said. "Should be fired tomorrow. Sorry, the whole staff. The whole staff."

Gus then took it a step further, saying that the post-game fireworks following Thursday night's embarrassing loss were a little off base.

"Fireworks? Forget about fireworks. We need a firing squad."

articles.title: Stuttgart bounce back from Bayern thrashing with win over Cologne
articles.summary: VfB Stuttgart bounced back from the thrashing by Bayern Munich in their Bundesliga opener with a 4-1 home win against Cologne on Friday evening. Stuttgart la...
articles.body:
VfB Stuttgart bounced back from the thrashing by Bayern Munich in their Bundesliga opener with a 4-1 home win against Cologne on Friday evening.

Stuttgart last week started the season with a hefty 5-1 defeat to the reigning league champions, but will have a much better weekend this time around.

Bilal El Khannouss took everything into his own hands to break the deadlock in the 39th minute.

He charged towards the goal and skipped past two defenders, seeing off the second one with a cheeky nutmeg, before sliding the ball into the goal.

Cologne brought in young English loan Mikey Moore, and he had an immediate impact on the match. The guests stepped up the pace and it really looked like they were going to find an equalizer.

But against the odds, it was Stuttgart who scored again. Maximilian Mittelstädt didn't let the ball go out and cut back to the centre of the box for newcomer Grischa Prömel to score his first goal for the club in the 60th.

Ermedin Demirovic added a third in the 75th from another great solo effort before Cologne at least pulled one back in the 81st thanks to Marius Bülter, who was assisted by Moore.

Before the final whistle, Josha Vagnoman completed the win with a stunning first-time shot in the 90th.

Cologne opened the season with a 3-2 win over Hoffenheim and are eighth in the standings, with Stuttgart one position ahead of them.

Saturday's Bundesliga schedule includes Hoffenheim v Borussia Dortmund, Bayer Leverkusen v Union Berlin and Schalke v Bayern Munich.

articles.title: UAlbany lets one slip at Buffalo as brutal future FBS schedule looms
articles.summary: Late miscues doom UAlbany at Buffalo ahead of future Power Four matchups.
articles.body:
BUFFALO - The wins over Football Bowl Subdivision teams will be much harder to come by over the next three years.

The University at Albany is set to play Purdue next season, Michigan State in 2028, and Cincinnati in 2029, according to an athletic department official.

Those games will offer big paydays but a slim chance of victory against teams from the Power Four conferences.

However, UAlbany had a realistic chance of pulling off an FBS upset on Thursday night. The Great Danes were sitting on the Buffalo 1 with less than two minutes left and trailing by 4 points.

Instead, UAlbany unraveled with mistakes in a 21-17 defeat in a game that didn't end until 1:22 a.m. because of lightning and heavy rain that delayed the opening kickoff by more than 2 ½ hours.

"We should have won that game," UAlbany first-year coach Tom Perkovich said. "We're on the 1-yard line, right?"

After the game, Perkovich was bent over in the tunnel to the locker room. He had his hands on his knees like he'd been punched in the gut.

These opportunities don't come along every year. Even though the Bulls of the Mid-American Conference don't nearly stack up against college football's best, it would have been a great victory for the Great Danes (1-1), who were 18 ½-point underdogs.

"We've got to find a way to win that game, that's what we've got to do," Perkovich said. "And I've got to do a better job as a head coach."

UAlbany fell to 1-11 against FBS opponents, the only win coming at Buffalo in 2016.

Nevertheless, Perkovich has taken over a team that went 2-10 last season and won his opener in impressive fashion against Coastal Athletic Association rival New Hampshire last Friday, followed by a near-upset of Buffalo despite the weather delay.

"Talk about facing adversity," Perkovich said. "We're in the hotel all day, right? We've got to sit here. We warm up; it takes over three hours to kick off. We're playing until 1:30 in the morning. Our guys went through a lot today. And to come here and have that type of effort and what we do, I'm proud of our players. We didn't get the win, but I'm proud of our guys."

Perkovich said he expressed that pride to his disappointed team in the locker room.

"What we're doing is working," Perkovich said he told the players. "We've got the right people. We can't let it destroy us, losing a game at the end like that. But we need to come together closer and continue to work toward getting some things fixed and get this thing in a better position where we're not down to the last seconds."

Through a UAlbany spokesman, Perkovich declined to make players available for interviews.

On the bright side, UAlbany senior quarterback Kai Colon showed his arm talent against Buffalo after doing most of his damage with his legs against UNH.

Colon threw for 191 yards and a pair of 14-yard touchdowns - the first to Tavahri Groves in the first quarter and the second to Justus Murray Jr. for a 17-14 lead with 3:23 left in the third quarter.

His most impressive throw was a 24-yard out to Jordan Rae on fourth-and-2 to the Buffalo 20 on UAlbany's final drive.

UAlbany's Rahshan La Mons was stopped just short of the goal line on a run to set up the final sequence. On second down, tight end Tyler Wilms false-started just before backup quarterback Aidan Semo took a snap and snuck into the end zone for what would have been the go-ahead score.

Wilms was lined up behind scrimmage and looked to give Semo a tush push into the end zone.

"It looked like we jumped the gun on it, so I don't know," Perkovich said.

The penalty marched UAlbany back to the 6. The Great Danes' last bid ended when Colon's fourth-down pass was caught over the middle by Shenendehowa graduate Luke McAuliffe, who was tackled at the 3 to turn the ball over on downs.

"I had a couple bad play calls that I've got to own and we've got to be better," said Perkovich, who is the offensive play caller. "We've got to go to the end zone on the last play. I think we had something, but we've got to go to the end zone on it."

UAlbany returns to action at Long Island University of the Northeast Conference on Sept. 12.

articles.title: TCU restores Fort Worth Star-Telegram credential pulled after reporting on locker room fight resulting in player's dismissal
articles.summary: TCU said it revoked the Star-Telegram's credential due to alleged threats made against the player attacked. Reporter Steven Johnson covered the Horned Frogs'...
articles.body:
The TCU football program has restored credentials for the Fort Worth Star-Telegram after the newspaper's access was revoked for its coverage of a locker room altercation that resulted in safety Jacob Fields being dismissed from the team .

"Today, TCU Athletics fully restored media credentials to the Fort Worth Star-Telegram," a statement issued by TCU said . "In a series of productive discussions, we made clear our position and resolved to move forward. We respect their role as an independent news source and voice in our community, and we look forward to the season ahead."

"Today, TCU Athletics fully restored media credentials to the Fort Worth Star-Telegram," a statement issued by TCU said .

"In a series of productive discussions, we made clear our position and resolved to move forward. We respect their role as an independent news source and voice in our community, and we look forward to the season ahead."

Star-Telegram reporter Steven Johnson reported on Aug. 18 that tensions had been developing in the locker room, but coaches made no attempts to de-escalate the situation despite being informed of what was happening. Head coach Sonny Dykes reportedly did not realize how serious the issues were among players.

After the Star-Telegram reported that its credentials had been pulled , a TCU athletic department spokesman said the decision was made because of alleged threats made to sophomore receiver Dozie Ezukanma, who had been punched by Fields. However, the newspaper's report of the incident did not identify Ezukanma until the player revealed he was the one attacked on a social media video.

Johnson traveled to Dublin, Ireland to cover TCU's 15-10 loss to North Carolina in its season opener, but did so from the stands rather than the press box at Aviva Stadium.

Jacob Fields dismissed from team after locker room fight

Fields was dismissed from the team earlier this month after the locker room fight. The incident in question occurred on Aug. 13.

Ezukanma alleged in an Instagram video that Fields "sucker punched" him, causing his head to hit the floor and knocking him unconscious. He said Fields also kicked him in the head, the Fort Worth Star-Telegram reported .

A TCU football staffer reported the incident to campus police the next day, according to an official report . Fields was subsequently dismissed from the football team and a warrant for Fields' arrest stated that Ezukanma suffered a brain bleed from the attack.

Fields was arrested on Aug. 30 after turning himself in to Tarrant County, Texas police on a charge of aggravated assault causing serious bodily injury. The senior transfer was booked into the Tarrant County Jail and was released later that day after posting a $50,000 bond .

articles.title: August’s Monthly Juventus Thoughts: Comeback Kids
articles.summary: The new season has started and another transfer window has closed. Are we in a better spot than last season? Let’s see!
articles.body:
A brutal summer of deadly heatwaves and extreme weather has passed. Maybe the heat got to some of the hearts and minds of European football executives because we saw some (cumulative) transfer fees that came close to the GDPs of small countries . Or perhaps the football industry has learned a lesson from the current AI bubble industry , which is to spend first and ask questions later.

Whatever the case, we can finally take a collective breath now that the transfer window has closed until January. Because transfers are pointless without the action that really matters: the football on the pitch.

Yes, my friends, the 2026-27 season has begun!

It was one of the busiest pre-seasons on the pitch for Juventus as we had four friendlies in August alone (and three in July). We beat Chelsea 1-0 thanks to a lovely goal from Edon Zhegrova — where was that against Gala, my friend? — but lost 2-1 to Inter in a game that essentially marked the end of Michele Di Gregorio's Juventus career. He could have reacted more sharply for Inter's first goal but completely flapped at the shot for Any Diouf's goal that doubled Inter's lead. Francisco Conceição scored the late consolation goal for the Bianconeri.

We then comfortably beat Palermo 2-0 thanks to goals from Kenan Yildiz and Arek Milik before the traditional annual friendly game between the senior team and the Next Gen team. The senior team was in the lead by two goals before an uncharacteristically early pitch invasion from the fans halted the game. Somewhat bizarrely, an overly enthusiastic fan injured Federico Gatti during the "festivities." These are strange times …

The real action started on Aug. 23: the season opener away from home against newly promoted Frosinone. It was a solid, if unspectacular victory as Gleison Bremer scored the game's only goal halfway through the first half after heading home from Conceição's cross. The Bianconeri restricted Frosinone to just two shots on target but never really seemed to kick into high gear on the other end of the pitch. A timid start to the season but a victory nonetheless.

It was a similarly low-key but quietly dominant victory in the second game of the season, at home versus Parma, although we scored more goals this time. The story of the game was the comeback of the rejects, as forgotten men Nico González and Teun Koopmeiners came off the bench to score in the second half. González unleashed a wicked shot from 20 meters that hit the post and had so much power to it that it came all the way back to him. The Argentine hit a rebound that deflected off a Parma defender and went into goal. This came after he forced goalkeeper Edoardo Corvi into a phenomenal save from a powerful volley just outside the box.

Koopmeiners put the cherry on top when he scored the team's second goal a few minutes before the final whistle. Man-of-the-match González won the ball deep in Parma territory and played the ball to Locatelli, who quickly passed to Koopmeiners. The Dutchman drilled a low shot into the far corner and through the legs of a Parma defender to seal a solid 2-0 victory for the team.

It's not a fireworks start to the season, but it'll do for now!

After a slow start to the transfer window, Juventus kicked into gear in August to secure some interesting signings. Most importantly, we finally resolved the goalkeeper saga, at least for one season …

We signed Colombian defender Jhon Lucumí from Bologna on a deal that is worth up to €22 million.

A few young midfielders left Juventus. Montenegrin midfielder Vasilije Adžić moves to Sassuolo on loan with option to buy, Fabio Miretti missed Dusan Vlahovic so much that he joined him at Besiktas (on loan with option to buy), and Adin Ličina joined Cremonese on loan (and immediately scored in the Coppa Italia! )

The much-maligned and polarizing Canadian striker Jonathan David joined Atletico Madrid on loan with an option to buy, likely a (temporary) replacement for the even-more polarizing Julian Alvarez who is indefinitely exiled from the squad after his even-even more controversial move to Barcelona collapsed. So much controversy!

The ridiculous goalkeeper saga has finally come to an end. Michele Di Gregorio joined Bournemouth, Mattia Perin joined Palermo, we signed Guglielmo Vicario on loan from Tottenham Hotspur, and backup goalkeeper Kamil Grabara joins the team on loan with option to buy from Wolfsburg. I don't remember the last time Juventus had its two goalkeepers be on loan but hey, these are crazy times.

We signed the impossibly tall Newcastle striker Nick Woltemade on a dry, season-long loan.

After seemingly being very close to signing for Juventus, Franck Kessie decided to rejoin Atalanta. We signed the Senegalese midfielder Pape Matar Sarr from Tottenham Hotspur on loan with obligation to buy (subject to a few conditions), an underrated signing that might prove to be a masterstroke.

Juventus Women played a lot of European football last month. First up was a second round Champions League qualification match versus Torreense from Portugal. After a goalless first half, Estela Carbonell and Ana Capeta scored in the second half to give Juventus a dominant lead. Jennie Lakip scored a late consolation goal for the visitors but it wasn't enough to spark the comeback: 2-1.

The Bianconere had to fight till the bitter end in the next Champions League qualification match against Hammarby from Sweden. Svea Rehnberg scored from a close range shot for the Swedes but Alba Redondo pounced on a loose ball in the box to equalize before half time. The game remained on a knife's edge in the second half as both teams canceled each other out and headed towards extra-time.

Japanese international and new signing Remina Chiba decided the game for us in extra-time with two fantastic goals. The first was a powerful left-footed shot from distance and she nodded home Carbonell's cross for her second. Final score: 3-1. Back in Italy, we beat Como 2-0 in the Serie A Women's Cup thanks to goals from Redondo and another from the in-form Chiba.

Our next opponents in the Champions League was Austrian side St Polten. Tatiana Pinto gave us the lead after she controlled Julia Bartel's deflected shot and scored with a controlled shot. Martina Rosucci scored from a magical right-footed shot from distance that flew into the top corner. Pinto scored her second of the match in the 80th minute to give the Bianconere a comfortable 3-0 victory.

We battled to a difficult 1-0 victory over Como in the second matchday of the Serie A Women's Cup. Lea Khelifi scored the game's only goal in the first half after a tidy assist from Emma Stolen Godo.

Besides all the transfers, the biggest story of the month was certainly the news that Kenan Yildiz had surgery on a broken foot and will be out of action for a few months. In addition to Khephren Thuram's surgery , this is a significant blow to the Bianconeri's creative abilities in attack.

When it comes to creativity in attack, it means that our options are now:

The inconsistent Conceição who, despite his talent, still lacks a final product and struggles to produce double-digit goal contributions in a season.

An Edon Zhegrova who is completely devoid of confidence (and likely on his way out of the club)

The admittedly solid and reliable Jeremie Boga.

The unexperienced teenager Kerim Alajbegovic who could prove to be a masterstroke but surely needs time to settle.

And the potentially rejuvenated Nico González.

(Potential wildcard: pushing Andrea Cambiaso further forward as a winger)

It leaves in a very uncertain position with our wingers. Best case, Conceição finally consistently produces assists and a few goals and either Boga or Alajbegovic do enough to ensure that the Portuguese winger doesn't have the sole responsibility of creating danger in attack. Worst case, Conceição blows hot and cold again, Alajbegovic takes too long to settle, Boga plays alright but not enough to lift the team, and González disappears back into obscurity.

Given that we certainly cannot rely on our center forwards for much (yet?), it's going to be a very unpredictable 2-3 months in the attacking department for Juventus. Thankfully, I feel pretty confident about the team's defensive abilities but it does look to me that the manner in which we won the first two games of the season will likely be the blueprint for the team for (at least) the short-term.

articles.title: Los 'niños' de Fàbregas hacen volar al Como: doblete de Diao y gol de Nico Paz
articles.standfirst: Se impusieron en Génova con una gran remontada... antes del estreno en Champions League
articles.summary: Se impusieron en Génova con una gran remontada... antes del estreno en Champions League
articles.body: A la espera de los nueve partidos que completan la jornada tres de la Serie A 2026-27, el Como 1907 puede decir que este viernes domirá como líder del 'Calcio'. Los de Fàbregas remontaron (1-4) en Génova y golearon para sumar su segunda victoria consecutiva a domicilio. Assane Diao fue la estrella con un doblete mientras Nico Paz y Baturina también dejaron su impronta con un gol. El Como de Cesc Fàbregas es una apisonadora y llega a su debut en Champions (próximo jueves ante el RB Leipzig) de la mejor forma posible. No les alteró lo más mínimo encajar el 1-0 a los 19' (Osmajic) en un gran contragolpe del Genoa. Once minutos después, ya había remontado. Y lo hizo de la mano de una línea de mediapuntas tremendamente joven: Nico Paz (21), Martin Baturina (23) y Assane Diao (20). El croata hizo el empate con un disparo desde fuera del área, el ex del Betis el segundo cazando una volea y el argentino, el tercero atacando muy bien el espacio y definiendo por la escuadra ante Bijlow. No cambió la dinámica en la segunda parte pese a que De Rossi cambió a línea de cuatro atrás. Al contrario, el Como se lució al contragolpe. Douvikas tuvo una gran ocasión de cabeza y Nico Paz mandó el balón al palo, pero fue Diao, otra vez, con doblete, el que cerró el triunfo a pase del debutante Moise Kean. El Como, que ha arrancado la Serie A con tres partidos de visitante por las obras en su estadio (obligatorias para que el Giuseppe Sinigaglia fuera válido en Liga de Campeones), volverá a su casa el jueves ante el Leipzig y el próximo lunes 14 ante el Parma. En este 'tour' italiano, solamente Udinese (1-1) les sacó un punto.
